speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any specific changes in your height growth pattern or hand/wrist structure recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient mentions partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly; could you describe the specific physical features you noticed regarding your height growth pattern or hand structure, such as broadening of the metacarpals? I also need to know if you or your family members have experienced fractures from minor trauma before the age of 30.

REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan
REQUEST TEST: Karyotype

speaker: Doctor
text: The bone density scan results appear normal, and regarding your growth pattern, have you noticed if your fingers or hands appear unusually wide or broad compared to your peers? Additionally, do you experience frequent headaches or vision changes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of delayed menarche, clitoromegaly, and partial labial fusion strongly suggests a disorder of androgen excess, likely Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia. Have you noticed any signs of virilization in your mother, such as excessive hair growth or deepening of the voice, given the history of hirsutism during her pregnancy? Also, could you tell me if you have experienced any abdominal pain or vomiting?

REQUEST TEST: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone
REQUEST TEST: 11-Deoxycortisol
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_ULtrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone: Elevated; 11-Deoxycortisol: Normal; Abdominal_Ultrasound: No adrenal masses identified.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

The significantly elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone level, combined with your clinical presentation of ambiguous genitalia, severe acne, delayed menarche, and a family history of hirsutism, confirms this diagnosis. The normal 11-deoxycortisol and lack of adrenal masses help rule out other causes like 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency or adrenal tumors. We should proceed with initiating glucocorticoid replacement therapy immediately.
